messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testDigitLimitConstructor` intends to create a BigFraction close to 1/2 with a max denominator of 10: `new BigFraction(0.5000000001, 10)`. The test fails because an overflow exception is thrown during this creation.

The constructor `BigFraction(double, int)` delegates to `BigFraction(double, double, int, int)` with default epsilon=0 and maxIterations=100.

In the detailed constructor `BigFraction(double value, double epsilon, int maxDenominator, int maxIterations)`, the fraction approximation uses a continued fraction expansion until the denominator exceeds maxDenominator or the error is less than epsilon or maxIterations is reached.

The algorithm keeps track of numerator/denominator pairs p_i/q_i and updates them iteratively. At each step, it checks for overflow conditions `if ((p2 > overflow) || (q2 > overflow))`. If an overflow is detected, it throws `FractionConversionException`.

However, the issue arises in edge cases when the input double is very close to a simple fraction with denominator <= maxDenominator but a floating-point rounding or iteration causes p2 or q2 to overflow before the algorithm terminates. According to the comments, if the overflow happens while the fraction is still close enough to the value, the code intends to return the last fraction found. But in the actual code, it just throws an exception without catching or handling this scenario.

Thus, the root cause is that the method throws a `FractionConversionException` on overflow in the loop without correctly handling near matches with a maxDenominator. The test triggers this case by using `0.5000000001` which is very close to `1/2` requiring only denominator `2` which is less than `10` but the approximator still overflows since p2 or q2 become too large before the algorithm stops.

Hence, the bug is the missing special handling of overflow cases when the last fraction is very close to the actual value and has denominator less than maxDenominator: instead of throwing an exception, that last valid fraction should be returned. The current code throws an exception directly causing the test failure.

This diagnosis aligns exactly with the bug report describing an overflow exception thrown when constructing a Fraction near a simple fraction with maxDenominator.

The faulty behavior is inside `BigFraction(double, double, int, int)` around lines 303-306.
org.apache.commons.math3.fraction.BigFraction.BigFraction(double, double, int, int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
